attributes.residual: COUNT PARITY, MEASURED AND QUOTED AS THE DECIDING FACT: insns 41/41 (ours/target), so this function is NOT count-asymmetric and a postprocessor class is not excluded by the count laws - it is excluded by the copy-form proof gap named below. TWO INDEPENDENT HALVES, and only one of them is a schedule problem. HALF ONE, +0x68/+0x6c: a clean adjacent transposition - ours emits `li r0,-1` then `stw r3,lbl_80344A24`, the target stores first. This is the SAME IDIOM as the already-shipped memCardErrorPrompt pin in this very TU ("ours materializes the argument `li r4,-1` before the SDA store, the target stores first"), and it is dependence-clean. HALF TWO, +0x14..+0x20: the live-zero copy-vs-remat class above. THE COMPOSED RULE REFUSES BECAUSE OF HALF TWO, NOT HALF ONE - copy_register_fields cannot rewrite a `li` into an `addi rD,rS,0` (that is a form change, not a register field, hence the 'base register presence differs (g3 vs g0)' refusal at +0x14), and equivalent_copy_form reports 'no proof mode offered' at +0x18 because no dominating definition of the zero reaches that site. So the function is refused by the postprocessor for a STATED reason and left to source. WHY THIS FUNCTION IS WORTH THE NEXT LANE'S TIME ANYWAY: it is the TU's only tier-B schedule row, its unabsorbed count is just 2 words in 1 cluster, and half one is provably closable - what blocks it is entirely half two. UNTRIED HYPOTHESIS: make the three zeroed locals share ONE definition that DOMINATES all uses, so equivalent_copy_form can offer `dominating_def` at +0x18 - e.g. hoist `zero = 0;` above the `pad` declaration block or seed the later globals from `zero` (`lbl_80344A24 = zero;`) so a single zero web dominates both the prologue copies and the later stores.

hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the target's own words were read: +0x14 is `addi r30,r0,0` (a materialised zero) and +0x18 / +0x1c are `addi r27,r30,0` / `addi r31,r30,0`, i.e. the target seeds ONE zero and copies it twice. Our build emits three independent `li` zeros at +0x18, +0x1c and +0x20. So the target demonstrably HAS the single-dominating-zero shape this hypothesis asks MWCC to produce; only the source spelling that reaches it is unknown.
hypothesis.statement: The composed rule refuses only because of the live-zero half. If the three prologue zeros can be made to share ONE dominating definition, equivalent_copy_form gains a `dominating_def` proof at +0x18, and the +0x68 transposition is already dependence-clean, so the existing composition would close the whole 41-instruction function with no new class. The concrete source form to try first: seed the later zero stores from the existing `zero` local (`lbl_80344A24 = zero; lbl_80344A20 = zero;` and likewise for `lbl_803449D4`/`lbl_803449DC`) so the zero web is live across the region rather than rematerialised per site.
